executive_summary.headline: DEMO (synthetic data): Egypt is the cheapest landed source at about 30% margin; China works at 19% but its quoted price sits above its usual export price; three other suppliers cannot be costed until prices and a duty rate arrive.
paragraphs: This is a demonstration study built entirely on synthetic data to show what the toolkit produces for an importer. None of its figures describe a real market.
In the synthetic data, Saudi Arabia imported USD 59.8 million of frozen vegetables (HS 071080) in 2025, growing 8.1% a year since 2022. Egypt is already its largest supplier with a 21.0% share.
At the quoted supplier prices and the importer's local selling price, Egypt lands at USD 1.04 per kg and earns 30.3%; China lands at USD 1.20 per kg and earns 19.4%, both above the 15% target.
Belgium, Spain and India cannot be costed yet: Belgium's duty rate and the Spanish and Indian supplier prices are missing.
recommendations: Keep Egypt as the main source: it is the cheapest landed supplier, with a firm freight quote and zero duty in this demonstration.
Negotiate with the Chinese supplier: its quote lands about 15.8% above China's average export price in the trade data.
Request prices from Spanish and Indian suppliers and verify Belgium's duty rate, then re-run the model to rank all five sources.
executive_summary.key_caveat: Only two of the five suppliers are fully costed; the ranking of the others depends on prices still to be collected.

paragraphs: The study covers HS 071080 (frozen vegetables not elsewhere specified) imported into Saudi Arabia. Trade data cover 2021 to 2026; 2026 is partial, so trends use 2022 to 2025.
Every price, freight and tariff figure carries its source and a tier.
bullets: Trade flows: synthetic Comtrade-shaped data generated for this demonstration.
Supplier prices: pro-forma quotes for Egypt and China; last season's price for Belgium.

paragraphs: Saudi Arabia's imports reached USD 59.8 million in 2025, ranking 10th among 47 reporting importers with a 2.41% world share.
bullets: All mirror checks are consistent: what suppliers report sending matches what Saudi Arabia reports receiving.

paragraphs: Reported world exports totalled USD 2,331 million in 2025. Spain is the largest exporter with an 18.5% share, followed by the Netherlands, China, Belgium and Poland.
Egypt supplies 21.0% of Saudi Arabia's imports, Belgium and India each under 3%, and China 0.7%, although China is the third-largest exporter worldwide.
Egypt and China have firm freight quotes. India's freight is a distance-based estimate with a wide range, and Belgium's comes from a rate tool.
Duty is zero for Egypt and Spain under an agreement in this demonstration; Belgium's rate is still to be verified.
bullets: India: the inland delivery cost in Saudi Arabia is missing for this lane.

paragraphs: Five suppliers were taken forward: four current sources to keep (Egypt, Belgium, Spain and India) and China to develop.

partner_notes.EGY: Largest current supplier; cheapest landed cost.
partner_notes.CHN: Large exporter with a small share of Saudi imports.
partner_notes.BEL: Established supplier; duty rate to be verified.
partner_notes.ESP: World's largest exporter; supplier price still needed.
partner_notes.IND: Supplier of interest; price and delivery cost still needed.

not_prioritised.reason: Large exporter, but much of its trade is likely re-exported product sourced elsewhere.

paragraphs: Buying FOB, the importer pays freight, insurance, duty and delivery. Egypt earns USD 10,845 per container (30.3%) and China USD 6,971 (19.4%).
The planned 24 containers a year would recover the one-time sourcing cost within 3 months at these margins.

partner_verdicts.CHN: Viable at target; negotiate the price down.
partner_verdicts.BEL: Not costed: duty rate to be verified.
partner_verdicts.IND: Not costed: supplier price and delivery cost needed.

diagnostic: Will Spanish and Indian suppliers quote below the Egyptian landed cost?
Can the Chinese supplier meet Saudi food registration requirements?
macro: Freight on the modelled India lane can move well outside its estimated range.
data_limits: All trade data in this demonstration are synthetic.
2026 is a partial year and is excluded from trends.

two_weeks: Request FOB quotes from two Spanish and two Indian suppliers.
Verify Belgium's duty rate with the customs broker.
thirty_days: Re-run the model with all five suppliers costed and choose a second source.
ninety_days: Place a trial order with the second source and compare the actual landed cost with the model.
